reforms.description: The U.S. government is shifting its focus from military R&D to civilian and dual-use technologies, aiming to improve the productivity of private R&D through federally-funded mission-oriented research. This includes a significant reallocation of federal R&D spending from defense-related projects to enhance productivity and competitiveness in high technology manufacturing industries.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The shift towards civilian and dual-use technologies is expected to enhance productivity and competitiveness in high technology sectors, supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform has been actively implemented since its announcement.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a structural change in federal R&D priorities, indicating a major shift in focus and funding.
reforms.source_quote: Too much of the nation's R&D spending has been devoted to defence-related projects, and direct federal outlays are set to shift to civilian and dual-use technologies.

reforms.description: The U.S. government proposed a major budgetary increase for the National Institute of Standards and Technology to support the Advanced Technology Program aimed at developing high-risk generic technologies. Additionally, a series of investment initiatives totaling $220 billion were proposed to stimulate economic growth across various sectors, including technology and worker training.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The proposed budget increase and investment initiatives are designed to foster innovation and economic growth, enhancing the technological capabilities of the U.S.
reforms.status_evidence: The proposals have been announced but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, these reforms are narrower in scope compared to major structural changes.
reforms.source_quote: The new Administration has also indicated a willingness to move toward greater activism by proposing a major budgetary increase ($535 million in FY 1994).

reforms.description: The Administration proposed to make the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit permanent, enhancing its effectiveness in promoting R&D activities. Additionally, the Defence Reinvestment and Conversion Initiative includes various programs aimed at easing the transition for defense workers and communities, fostering partnerships between industry and national laboratories for dual-use technology.
reforms.package_name: Tax Credit and Defence Conversion Initiative
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Making the tax credit permanent is expected to provide stable support for R&D activities, while the conversion initiative aims to facilitate innovation and economic adaptation in affected communities.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiatives have been implemented as part of the Administration's policy.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant reform in innovation policy, impacting both tax incentives and defense sector transitions.
reforms.source_quote: The Administration proposed to make the credit permanent which would have served to enhance its effectiveness, but Congress extended it only through June 1995.

reforms.description: The Administration intends to promote 'Regional Technology Alliances' and 'Agile Manufacturing Programs' to assist in the exploitation of network externalities and stimulate technology transfer. Additionally, the proposed establishment of technology outreach or extension centres aims to facilitate the diffusion and exploitation of existing technologies between national laboratories and private industry.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These initiatives are designed to enhance collaboration between public and private sectors, facilitating the transfer and commercialization of technology, which is vital for economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiatives have been actively implemented since their announcement.
reforms.importance_rationale: While important for technology transfer, these initiatives are more focused and do not represent a major overhaul of the system.
reforms.source_quote: The Administration intends to promote 'Regional Technology Alliances' and 'Agile Manufacturing Programs' in order to assist in the exploitation of network externalities, and technology outreach or extension centres to stimulate technology transfer.

reforms.description: The Administration proposed a comprehensive overhaul of the health-care system, aiming for near-universal coverage through managed competition and state-based cooperatives, which is expected to require additional spending of about $35 billion per year.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The proposed overhaul aims to improve health care access and quality, which can enhance the productivity of the workforce.
reforms.status_evidence: The proposal has been announced but not yet legislated.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant structural change in the health care system, impacting a large segment of the population.
reforms.source_quote: The reform proposes a form of managed competition, rather than any kind of single-payer system.
